history: match-crash.json (internal_failure only): fixed-in v1.7.2308 (2023-08-14), last-repro'd v1.7.2212.1 (2023-03-01) -- the crash was already fixed before the issue was filed (2023-10-03), consistent with the reporter's CE pin (dxc_1_7_2207, 2022-07-18) being stale. match.json (internal_failure OR contains 'casting to type void unimplemented'): always-repro'd across every probeable release v1.7.2207..v1.9.2607 (5 pre-2022 releases invalid-probe due to -HV 202x/ps_6_7 requirements, 5 prereleases excluded by policy), plus main-debug. Attributed to PR #8079 (merged df50f51f8, 2026-01-26, 'Fixes #5823'), which stops SPIR-V codegen for the un-instantiated template-declaration VarDecl via CXXRecordDecl::getDescribedClassTemplate() -- non-null only for a primary template's pattern record, so it never matches a ClassTemplatePartialSpecializationDecl. Confirmed by reproducing PR #8079's own regression test (variant-primary-template-fix-test.hlsl, exit 0) and by the partial-specialization repro still hitting the pre-fix codepath (out-main-debug.txt).

summary: The reported SIGSEGV is fixed (PR #8079, v1.7.2308-equivalent fix for the crash symptom): the exact 2023 repro now exits 0x80004005 with 'casting to type void unimplemented' instead of crashing. But the underlying defect persists and is broader than reported: (1) any out-of-line definition of a class-template partial-specialization's static member still fails to compile at all, because PR #8079's fix only detects primary-template declaration context, not partial-specialization context; (2) separately, full/explicit-specialization and even plain (non-specialized) template static members only compile out-of-line if the illegal, C++-invalid duplicated 'static' keyword is kept -- dropping it (the standards-correct spelling) is misparsed as a new in-class field and rejected with ''const' is not a valid modifier for a field', matching devshgraphicsprogramming's 2025-12-10 comment on the related, closed #6677; (3) DXC never diagnoses that illegal duplicated 'static', unlike Clang, which rejects the equivalent C++ construct. #6677's narrower ask (generic C++11-style deduced OOL initializers) was correctly closed NOT_PLANNED as a template-model feature gap per llvm-beanz -- that specific ask is out of scope here, but the bogus 'const' diagnostic reproduces even for a full/explicit specialization where no deduction is involved, so it is a genuine parser bug, not a feature gap.
